# manifest — Repository boundary manifest — provides/consumes schema and rivet manifest export

# Repository boundary manifest

The embedded `manifest` schema describes what a repository ships to other
repositories (`provides`) and what it pins from them (`consumes`).
`rivet manifest export --format json` turns those artifacts into
`pulseengine.manifest.json`, a document that conforms to the JSON Schema
committed at `schemas/pulseengine.manifest.v1.json`
(`schema_version: "pulseengine.manifest/1"`).

## Enabling the schema

List `manifest` in `rivet.yaml`, or pick it at init time:

```bash
rivet init --preset dev --schema common,dev,manifest
```

```yaml
project:
  name: my-repo
  schemas:
    - common
    - dev
    - manifest
```

## `provides`

| Field | Required | Notes |
|-------|----------|-------|
| `kind` | yes | `crate`, `component`, `wit-package`, `release-asset`, `proof-target`, `bazel-target`, `required-check`, `contract`, `tool`, `oci` |
| `entry-id` | yes | The deliverable's identifier (crate name, package, label…). Exported as `id`; `id` itself is the rivet artifact id. |
| `version` | yes | Version of the deliverable. |
| `path` / `oci` | per kind | Locator. Every kind except `required-check` needs one. |
| `workspace` | `crate` | `root` or `nested` |
| `index`, `world` | `component` (optional) | Component index and WIT world |
| `asset` | `release-asset` | Release asset file name |
| `backend` | `proof-target` | `kani`, `verus`, `rocq`, `lean` |
| `mode` | `bazel-target` | `must-build` or `waived`; a waived target also needs `waiver` (the issue link) |
| `context` | `required-check` | The CI status-check context name |
| `contract` | `contract` | `seam`, `wire-binding`, `table` (its version is `version`) |
| `required-checks` | no | Gate binding: CI check contexts that must pass |

Gate binding: a `gated-by` link from a `provides` artifact names a
verification artifact (a test, proof, review…) that backs it.

## `consumes`

| Field | Required | Notes |
|-------|----------|-------|
| `repo` | yes | Upstream repository |
| `entry-id` | yes | The upstream deliverable's id (its `provides[].id`) |
| `pin` | yes | Mapping `{kind, value}`: `kind` is `tag`, `rev`, `sha256`, `path+ref` or `oci`; `value` must not be empty |

## Example

```yaml
artifacts:
  - id: PROV-001
    type: provides
    title: core crate
    status: approved
    fields:
      kind: crate
      entry-id: my-core
      version: 0.1.0
      path: crates/my-core
      workspace: nested
      required-checks: [ci / test]
    links:
      - type: gated-by
        target: REQ-001
  - id: CONS-001
    type: consumes
    title: upstream analysis crate
    status: approved
    fields:
      repo: pulseengine/spar
      entry-id: spar-analysis
      pin: {kind: tag, value: v0.1.0}
```

## What `rivet validate` checks

Besides the generic checks (`required-field` for a `provides` without
`version` or a `consumes` without `pin`), these rules report an ERROR, so
`rivet validate` exits 1:

| Rule | Fires when |
|------|------------|
| `manifest-kind` | `kind` is not one of the kinds above |
| `manifest-kind-field` | a kind-specific field is missing (`workspace` on a crate, `waiver` on a waived bazel-target, …) |
| `manifest-enum` | `workspace`, `backend`, `mode` or `contract` holds a value outside its set |
| `manifest-locator` | neither `path` nor `oci` is set on a kind that needs a locator |
| `manifest-pin` | `pin` is not a mapping, `pin.kind` is missing or unknown, or `pin.value` is missing or empty |
| `manifest-empty` | `entry-id`, `version` or `repo` is present but empty |

## `rivet manifest export`

```bash
rivet manifest export --format json                      # print to stdout
rivet manifest export --output pulseengine.manifest.json # write a file
rivet manifest export --output dist/ --repo pulseengine/my-repo --tag v0.1.0
```

- `--output` writes the file (a directory gets `pulseengine.manifest.json`
  inside it); without it the document goes to stdout.
- `--repo` sets `repo` (default: the project name in `rivet.yaml`).
- `--tag` sets `release.tag` (default: `null`).

The document has six top-level fields: `schema_version`, `repo`,
`release {tag}`, `provides[]`, `consumes[]` and `gates[]`. Each `provides` /
`consumes` entry carries every field set on its artifact (with `entry-id`
written as `id`), plus `artifact` (the rivet id) and `title`. Scalars in
string fields are written as strings, so `version: 1` exports as `"1"`.
`gates[]` flattens the gate bindings: one record per `gated-by` link
(`kind: artifact`, with the target's `type` and `status`) and one per
`required-checks` entry (`kind: required-check`).

Exit codes: `0` exported; `1` a `provides` / `consumes` artifact has a
validation error (the errors go to stderr and nothing is written); `2` usage —
an unknown flag or `--format` value, or a project that does not load the
`manifest` schema.

Out of scope: cross-repository checks (does the pinned upstream really
provide the id?) — the manifest is the input those checks will read.

---

## Schema source (`schemas/manifest.yaml`)

# Repository manifest schema (rivet#1159).
#
# Describes a repository's BOUNDARY: what it ships to other repositories
# (`provides`) and what it pins from them (`consumes`). `rivet manifest
# export --format json` turns the artifacts of these two types into a
# `pulseengine.manifest.json` document conforming to
# `schemas/pulseengine.manifest.v1.json` (schema_version
# "pulseengine.manifest/1").
#
#   provides  — one deliverable this repo publishes: a crate, a WebAssembly
#               component, a WIT package, a release asset, a proof target, a
#               Bazel target, a required CI check, a contract, a tool or an
#               OCI image. Gate binding: `gated-by` links name the
#               verification artifacts that back it; `required-checks` names
#               the CI check contexts that must pass for it.
#   consumes  — one upstream deliverable this repo depends on, with the
#               exact pin: {kind: tag|rev|sha256|path+ref|oci, value}.
#
# Field naming: the manifest entry's identifier is the `entry-id` field
# (`id` is reserved for the rivet artifact id); export writes it as `id`.
#
# What YAML alone cannot express is enforced by rivet-core's
# `manifest::validate_manifest` and fails `rivet validate` with an ERROR:
#   - `kind` outside the enum below                     (manifest-kind)
#   - a kind-specific field missing, e.g. a `crate`
#     without `workspace`, or a waived `bazel-target`
#     without a `waiver` issue link                    (manifest-kind-field)
#   - a kind-specific enum value outside its set        (manifest-enum)
#   - no locator (`path` or `oci`) where the kind
#     needs one                                         (manifest-locator)
#   - `pin` not a mapping, `pin.kind` missing or
#     outside the enum, `pin.value` missing or empty    (manifest-pin)
#   - `entry-id` / `version` / `repo` present but empty (manifest-empty)
# `required: true` fields below are enforced by the generic
# `required-field` check (a `provides` without `version`, a `consumes`
# without `pin`).

schema:
  name: manifest
  version: "0.1.0"
  extends: [common]
  description: >
    Repository boundary manifest: `provides` (what this repo ships) and
    `consumes` (what it pins from other repos). Exported as
    pulseengine.manifest.json by `rivet manifest export`.

# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Artifact types
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
artifact-types:

  - name: provides
    description: >
      One deliverable this repository publishes to other repositories.
      `kind` selects which kind-specific fields apply (see the field
      descriptions). Gate binding: link the verification artifacts that
      back the deliverable with `gated-by`, and list the CI check contexts
      that must pass for it in `required-checks`.
    fields:
      - name: kind
        type: string
        required: true
        allowed-values:
          - crate
          - component
          - wit-package
          - release-asset
          - proof-target
          - bazel-target
          - required-check
          - contract
          - tool
          - oci
        description: >
          What is provided. crate (needs `workspace`), component (optional
          `index`, `world`), wit-package, release-asset (needs `asset`),
          proof-target (needs `backend`), bazel-target (needs `mode`; a
          waived target needs `waiver`), required-check (needs `context`),
          contract (needs `contract`), tool, oci (needs `oci`). Every kind
          except required-check needs a locator (`path` or `oci`).
      - name: entry-id
        type: string
        required: true
        description: >
          The deliverable's identifier as consumers name it — crate name,
          component / package name, asset name, Bazel label, check name.
          Exported as the manifest entry's `id`.
      - name: version
        type: string
        required: true
        description: Version of the deliverable (crate version, WIT package version, contract version).
      - name: path
        type: string
        required: false
        description: Locator — repository-relative path of the deliverable.
      - name: oci
        type: string
        required: false
        description: Locator — OCI reference (e.g. ghcr.io/org/name:tag or @sha256:…).
      - name: workspace
        type: string
        required: false
        allowed-values: [root, nested]
        description: "kind: crate — whether the crate is the workspace root or a nested member."
      - name: index
        type: string
        required: false
        description: "kind: component — component index / registry the component is published to."
      - name: world
        type: string
        required: false
        description: "kind: component — WIT world the component targets."
      - name: asset
        type: string
        required: false
        description: "kind: release-asset — release asset file name."
      - name: backend
        type: string
        required: false
        allowed-values: [kani, verus, rocq, lean]
        description: "kind: proof-target — proof backend."
      - name: mode
        type: string
        required: false
        allowed-values: [must-build, waived]
        description: "kind: bazel-target — must-build, or waived (then `waiver` is required)."
      - name: waiver
        type: string
        required: false
        description: "kind: bazel-target with mode waived — link to the issue that tracks the waiver."
      - name: context
        type: string
        required: false
        description: "kind: required-check — the CI status-check context name."
      - name: contract
        type: string
        required: false
        allowed-values: [seam, wire-binding, table]
        description: "kind: contract — contract shape (its version is `version`)."
      - name: required-checks
        type: list<string>
        required: false
        description: >
          Gate binding — CI status-check context names that must pass for
          this deliverable. Exported into the manifest's `gates[]`.
    link-fields:
      - name: gated-by
        link-type: gated-by
        cardinality: zero-or-many
        description: >
          Gate binding — verification artifacts (tests, proofs, reviews)
          that back this deliverable. Exported into the manifest's
          `gates[]`.
    example: |
      - id: PROV-001
        type: provides
        title: rivet-core crate
        status: approved
        fields:
          kind: crate
          entry-id: rivet-core
          version: 0.1.0
          path: rivet-core
          workspace: nested
          required-checks: [ci / test]
        links:
          - type: gated-by
            target: REQ-001

  - name: consumes
    description: >
      One upstream deliverable this repository depends on, pinned
      exactly. `pin.kind` is one of tag, rev, sha256, path+ref, oci;
      `pin.value` is the pinned value and must not be empty.
    fields:
      - name: repo
        type: string
        required: true
        description: Upstream repository (e.g. pulseengine/spar).
      - name: entry-id
        type: string
        required: true
        description: >
          The upstream deliverable's identifier, matching the upstream
          manifest's `provides[].id`. Exported as the entry's `id`.
      - name: pin
        type: mapping
        required: true
        description: >
          The exact pin, as a mapping with keys `kind` (tag | rev | sha256 |
          path+ref | oci) and `value` (non-empty). Checked by the
          `manifest-pin` rule.
    link-fields: []
    example: |
      - id: CONS-001
        type: consumes
        title: spar analysis crate
        status: approved
        fields:
          repo: pulseengine/spar
          entry-id: spar-analysis
          pin: {kind: tag, value: v0.1.0}

# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Link types
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
link-types:
  - name: gated-by
    inverse: gates
    description: >
      A provided deliverable is backed by the target verification artifact
      (gate binding). The deliverable should not ship unless the target
      holds.
    source-types: [provides]
